required_floor_classes.lane_definition: An international-affairs scenario cannot pass if consular access, diplomatic presence, humanitarian reach, development-program reach, security-assistance access, exchange access, or financial-instrument availability falls below reviewed component-specific floors.

An international-affairs scenario cannot pass if lower costs degrade diplomatic effectiveness, humanitarian timeliness, development quality, security-assistance controls, personnel safety, financial-instrument risk controls, or statutory compliance.

An international-affairs scenario cannot pass if burden, service loss, protection loss, humanitarian exclusion, development exclusion, or financial risk shifts by recipient, region, crisis type, income, displacement status, security exposure, or vulnerability without review.

An international-affairs scenario cannot pass if diplomatic continuity, humanitarian response capacity, development continuity, security-assistance control capacity, exchange continuity, or financial-instrument resilience falls below reviewed floors.

An international-affairs scenario cannot pass without separate diplomacy, ODA/development, humanitarian, security, exchange, and financial-instrument paths; commitment-to-outlay bridge; recipient/instrument/purpose decomposition; implementation cost; risk control; and delivery feasibility.

international_affairs_specific_floor_def.definition: Diplomatic operations, consular services, foreign-affairs conduct, personnel safety, and continuity require sourced floors before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Official-development-assistance scope, development outcomes, recipient purpose, and implementation quality require matched peer and program floors.
Humanitarian reach, timeliness, crisis coverage, protection, and continuity require explicit reviewed floors.
Security-assistance outcomes, end-use controls, partner risk, statutory restrictions, and oversight require sourced floors before policy scoring.

Foreign Military Sales, credit, exchange-stabilization, IMF, Ex-Im, trust-fund, collection, and credit-accounting effects require separate instrument paths and cannot be treated as negative aid, fraud recovery, or automatic savings.

No target cost can be selected without separate component policy paths, commitment-to-outlay bridge, recipient/instrument/purpose decomposition, matched peer scope, implementation cost, risk controls, and delivery feasibility.

public_warning_phrases: This international-affairs floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.
The negative international financial-program entry is trust-fund, collection, and credit accounting; it is not negative diplomacy, negative foreign aid, fraud recovery, or automatic savings.
Diplomacy, ODA/development, humanitarian response, security assistance, information/exchange, and financial instruments must remain separate.

No lower-cost international-affairs scenario is admissible until diplomacy/consular presence, ODA/development effectiveness, humanitarian response, security-assistance controls, financial-instrument risk/accounting, component-commitment-outlay, equity, adequacy/resilience, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not a diplomacy path, not an ODA path, not a humanitarian path, not a security-assistance path, not a financial-instrument path, not a commitment-to-outlay bridge, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
